questionText:
Read the following case study on adolescent public health nutrition and answer the questions that follow:

During an annual health screening at a government girls' senior secondary school, the medical team tests hemoglobin levels across 300 adolescent girls. Teachers report that many anemic students experience chronic lethargy, difficulty concentrating in class, frequent headaches, and poor academic scores. Physical inspection demonstrates conjunctival pallor and pale nail beds. The school implements the national 'Anemia Mukt Bharat' protocol:
1. Administering Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFAS) using blue IFA tablets (100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) on fixed days (Wednesdays).

topic: Thermal Food Processing Methods and Parameters
questionText:
Match the thermal process in List I with its operational definition in List II:

List I:
(A) Blanching
(B) Pasteurization
(C) Sterilization
(D) Ultra-High Temperature (UHT)

List II:
(I) Mild heat treatment (85-95°C) of vegetables to inactivate enzymes prior to freezing
(II) Heat treatment below 100°C to destroy vegetative pathogens and extend refrigerated shelf life
(III) Severe heat treatment (>100°C) destroying all viable microorganisms and bacterial spores
(IV) Thermal processing at 135-150°C for 1 to 2 seconds for aseptic packaging and room-temperature storage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Blanching inactivates enzymes, pasteurization kills vegetative pathogens, sterilization destroys all microbes/spores, and UHT enables shelf-stable aseptic milk.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.

questionText: [Set 33.34] In pediatric clinical assessment, Kwashiorkor is clinically distinguished from Marasmus by the prominent presence of:

options.text: Oedema (fluid accumulation in legs and face) and enlarged fatty liver with adequate calorie intake but acute protein deficiency
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus.

options.text: Severe muscle wasting and subcutaneous fat depletion without oedema (skin and bone appearance)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Vitamin C scurvy bleeding gums exclusively
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Excessive subcutaneous adipose tissue and childhood obesity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus (Nutrition, Food Science and Technology):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Public Nutrition and Health - Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus):
Kwashiorkor is caused by acute protein deficiency despite sufficient caloric intake, leading to generalized oedema, enlarged fatty liver, lethargy, and a 'moon face'. Marasmus is total protein-energy malnutrition characterized by severe wasting without oedema.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Pasteurization of Milk (HTST Method) (Nutrition, Food Science and Technology):

According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Food Processing and Technology - Pasteurization of Milk (HTST Method)):
HTST pasteurization heats milk to $71.7^\circ\text{C}$ ($161^\circ\text{F}$) for 15 seconds, which destroys pathogenic vegetative microorganisms (e.g., Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Coxiella burnetii) without impairing milk flavor.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.
